source_title: Civilization #5:  The Yamnaya Conquest of Europe
summary: This Yamnaya lecture is already-public source support for Civilization As Inner Order: steppe pastoralism turns grass into cattle wealth, private property, primogeniture, young-male violence, mobility, and Sky Father religion, creating a coherent conquest order that replaces Old Europe.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: The lecture shows material survival, property, inheritance, violence, sex, religion, and status changing together when cattle wealth becomes the organizing fact of steppe life.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The public Civilization page already cites this source in its definition anchor because the active mechanism is a whole lived order, not only one technology or migration.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Mother Goddess interconnection is replaced by Sky Father wealth and war, showing that sacred order can protect harmony or authorize domination.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The source gives the sharp contrast between the Old Europe / Mother Goddess order and the pastoral property-war order already carried by Civilization.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Cattle, milk, horses, wagons, private property, primogeniture, patriarchy, expansionary violence, and Sky Father religion form one aligned conquest package.
existing_lens_links.rationale: This is the lecture's strongest public anchor. The Civilization page already exposes it as the Yamnaya mechanism where economy, sex, inheritance, violence, and religion change at once.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: The lecture supplies the full pastoral-conquest explanation after the prior Old Europe / Gimbutas setup: mobile cattle wealth, horse and wagon movement, younger-son raiding, plague-weakened farmers, and gendered replacement.
existing_lens_links.rationale: Pastoral Conquest can use this as definition-spine support, but the public concept home remains Civilization unless later sources require a narrower public page.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Already public: keep this source as the Steppe Rearranges Reality layer inside Civilization As Inner Order. The source shows grassland ecology becoming cattle wealth, cattle wealth becoming private property and inheritance, inheritance producing surplus sons and raiding, and Sky Father religion making wealth-war morally coherent.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Civilization As Inner Order owns the whole-package replacement of one lived world by another. Power gets only bounded property/money pressure; Borderland gets only the open-competition/outside-borrower comparison; Strategy gets only later war-form comparison; Nation or Eschatology should not absorb the source from the West / Sky Father language alone.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold the open cooperative competition material as boundary pressure only: Jiang defines innovation as coming from many groups competing, trading, intermarrying, and learning without one central authority, then says the ruthless marginal borrower can become hegemon. The Borderland page already carries this mechanism through Qin, Macedon, Vikings, Mongols, and other stronger cases.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Borderland owns margin pressure, openness, cohesion, and captured innovation. This lecture remains Civilization-primary because the decisive public mechanism is not marginality by itself but an entire steppe order reorganizing property, sex, war, and religion.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold cattle-as-private-property and wealth-as-Sky-Father-gift as bounded early power pressure: cattle become ownable, inheritable, stealable wealth, and money enters the lecture as part of a new sacred order. This is not yet the Power page's main alchemy mechanism of invented abstraction commanding modern reality.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Power As Alchemy should not absorb this source unless a later comparison needs the origin layer of property and money. Here wealth is one element inside a whole pastoral conquest order.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold horse, wagon, mobility, body size, plague exposure, and gendered violence as weak comparison pressure for war-form material tests. The Strategy page already has stronger war-form examples; this source's war mechanism is civilizational replacement rather than modern strategic audit.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Strategy owns whether a war story survives material form. The Yamnaya source belongs first to Civilization because the material form and sacred order are inseparable in the lecture.

new_lens_seeds.title: Pastoral Conquest As Inner-Order Replacement
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: A pastoral conquest order becomes durable when ecology, food conversion, animal wealth, mobility, inheritance, male status, raiding incentives, and sacred justification align strongly enough to replace another people's family, property, gender, religious, and historical world.
new_lens_seeds.reuse_potential: The seed could later compare Yamnaya, Mongols, Vikings, Rome, and other conquest orders where mobility and marginal pressure reorganize a settled center, but the current public Civilization page already carries the Yamnaya mechanism without needing a child page.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Hold this as a routing seed, not a public page. A future child would need multiple dated sources proving a narrower mechanism than Civilization's existing steppe section and Borderland's existing margin-pressure page.

new_lens_seeds.title: Ruthless Borrower Wins Open Competition
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: Open, cooperative competition produces innovation across many groups, but the final hegemon may be the marginal actor most willing to borrow innovations and use them for destruction.
new_lens_seeds.reuse_potential: The seed can help compare Yamnaya, Macedon, Akkad, Qin, Vikings, Mongols, and later imperial borrowers, but the Borderland page already has stronger public machinery for this diagnostic.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Hold for later Borderland comparison. Do not create a standalone concept from this source alone because the public Borderland Engine already owns the broader marginal-borrower mechanism.

chronology_notes.note: Dated 2024-09-12, this source follows the 2024-09-10 Old Europe / Gimbutas lecture and supplies the conquest half of the pair: the Mother Goddess counter-order is not merely displaced by outsiders, but by a coherent pastoral package where cattle, mobility, private property, inheritance, masculinity, violence, and Sky Father religion make a new world.

This lecture turns the prior Kurgan / Old Europe setup into a full pastoral-conquest model. Preserve Jiang's distinction that Yamnaya spread is a culture and package of practices rather than one simple people moving uniformly.

Jiang defines the West in this lecture as the connected Indo-European zone from Europe through Iran and India, trading ideas, people, and gods, while China is spared by geography and remains comparatively isolated. Treat this as dated 2024 course framing, not as a standalone West or China concept.

The lecture contains broad historical and archaeological claims about Yamnaya origin, migration, plague, population replacement, India/Iran/Mongolia spread, and body-size effects. Preserve the source date and Jiang-attribution rather than turning these into unstated settled archaeology.

next_actions.action: No immediate public prose mutation is required: Civilization As Inner Order already cites this source, exposes the durable `civilization-inner-order-changes-together` lens point, and remains below split pressure at about 3,461 words, 8 local video slugs, and 7 stable anchors.

Do not create standalone Yamnaya, Proto-Indo-European, Pastoral Conquest, Sky Father, Cattle Wealth, Primogeniture, Younger Sons, Horse And Wheel, Steppe Innovation, Ruthless Borrower, The West, Indo-European West, China Saved By Geography, Plague Destroyed Old Europe, or War Money And The West pages from this source alone.
